title: Positive roots admit simple-root chains
statement: Let $I$ be finite and let $M,N$ be vector spaces over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field]. Let $P:\mathrm{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ M\ N$ be a crystallographic root pairing in the Mathlib sense: injective root and coroot families with a bilinear pairing, root-coroot value $2$, simultaneous root and coroot reflection permutations, and integral root-coroot pairings. Let $b:P.\mathrm{Base}$, so its support $D\subseteq I$ has linearly independent root and coroot families, and each root and each coroot or its negative is a nonnegative integral sum of the respective family on $D$. Write $a_i=P.\mathrm{root}(i)$ and call $i$ positive when the sum of its integral $D$-coordinates is positive. For every positive $i$ there exist $n\in\mathbf N$ and $f:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to I$ such that $f(m)\in D$ for every $m$, $a_i=\sum_{m=0}^{n-1}a_{f(m)}$, and $\sum_{r=0}^{m}a_{f(r)}\in\operatorname{range}(P.\mathrm{root})$ for every $0\leq m<n$.
